summary: Describes an allocation plan for IPv6 addresses used to test prototype IPv6 software, as used by the early test network. It is now historic, replaced by RFC 3701.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 2471 allocates temporary IPv6 addresses for testing prototype software on the 6bone. The addresses were not intended for normal Internet routing, and users were expected to renumber later.

questions: what was the ipv6 testing address allocation
how did ipv6 testbeds allocate addresses
what was the 6bone test address prefix

subtitle: Temporary IPv6 addresses for testing prototype software on the 6bone.

tldr.problem: IPv6 prototype software needed an address allocation for testing that was separate from ordinary Internet routing.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC assigns the 6bone testbed a temporary TLA ID of 0x1FFE within the aggregatable global unicast address format.
tldr.outcome: RFC 2471 is Historic and was replaced by RFC 3701; users of the temporary addresses were required to renumber.

today: RFC 2471 is Historic and was obsoleted by RFC 3701, according to the unit metadata.

sections.title: Temporary Addresses for Testing
sections.content: RFC 2471 describes an allocation plan for IPv6 addresses used to test prototype software. The addresses are temporary, will be reclaimed, and require systems using them to renumber in the future. They are not routable on the Internet except for IPv6 testing.
sections.plainLanguage: The address space is for IPv6 tests, not permanent network use. Systems using it must be ready to change addresses later.

sections.title: The 6bone Address Format
sections.content: The address format follows the aggregatable global unicast format. The RFC assigns TLA ID 0x1FFE for 6bone testing. The NLA ID identifies transit networks and end-user sites in the testbed hierarchy; each organization uses its SLA ID field to create a local hierarchy and identify subnets.
sections.plainLanguage: The address contains fields for the 6bone, network sites, local subnets, and an interface. Organizations manage their own site-level part.

sections.title: Assignment and Renumbering
sections.content: The 0x1FFE TLA ID is temporary and is administered by the chair of the 6bone activity. Addresses may be assigned manually, through IPv6 autoconfiguration, or with DHCP for IPv6. The RFC states that all users of the addresses will have to renumber at some time in the future.
sections.plainLanguage: The 6bone activity chair administers this temporary allocation. Users can configure addresses in several ways, but all must eventually renumber.
